studies.title: Jayhawk Wind Energy Project (Bourbon and Crawford Counties, Kansas): economic development report, November 2019
studies.method: JEDI Wind with 2017 IMPLAN state multipliers and the project's own spending and local shares; 25-year life
studies.published_words: 634 (190 direct) local jobs during construction for the State of Kansas; 43 (9 direct) long-term jobs for the State of Kansas; over $36.7 million in local earnings during construction for the State of Kansas; over $2.2 million in local long-term earnings; over $98.2 million in local output during construction; over $7.5 million in local long-term output

studies.title: Glendive Wind (Prairie County, Montana), NextEra Energy Resources: economic impact summary of a 2024 study by Strategic Economic Research
studies.method: IMPLAN multipliers with NREL's JEDI model, statewide
studies.published_words: Approx. 400 construction jobs in the state of Montana
studies.cost_words: $1 billion investment in Prairie County; up to 800 megawatts

studies.title: Measuring the Economic Impacts of Utility-Scale Solar in Ohio, Ohio University (Voinovich School), 31 July 2020: the low scenario
studies.method: JEDI PV updated with 2018 IMPLAN multipliers and NREL's Q1 2018 one-axis tracker utility cost benchmark; 80 percent Ohio labor and 30 percent Ohio materials; DC capacity; 2018 dollars; 40-year life
studies.published_words: a total of 18,039 one-time construction phase jobs, and 207 annual operations and maintenance (O&M) phase jobs; 8,536 direct construction jobs; roughly $3.2B construction phase economic impacts; up to $22.5M in annual tax revenues
studies.cost_words: Project Construction or Installation Cost, Low (2.5 GW): $3,592,192,939

studies.title: Economic Impacts from Indiana's First 1,000 Megawatts of Wind Power, NREL/TP-6A20-60914 (Tegen, Keyser and Flores-Espino, 2014)
studies.method: JEDI Wind with the seven projects' own expenditures and local shares (1,339 MW built 2008 to 2011; about 20 percent of construction spending and 40 percent of O&M in Indiana), results per 1,000 MW in 2010 real dollars
studies.published_words: Supported employment totaling more than 4,400 full-time-equivalent (FTE) jobs in Indiana during the construction periods; Supports approximately 260 ongoing Indiana jobs; Generates more than $8 million in annual property taxes (per 1,000 MW)
studies.cost_words: Table 3: construction expenditure USD 2,487 million for the 1,339 MW analyzed (equipment 1,830, materials 331, construction labor 159, development and other 167), scaled to 1,000 MW

studies.title: Economic Impacts from Wind Energy in Colorado, Case Study: Rush Creek Wind Farm, NREL/TP-5000-73659 (2019)
studies.method: JEDI Wind with the project's known costs from Xcel Energy's PUC filings and JEDI's default shares for the rest; Vestas's Colorado turbine factories in the supply chain; 2018 dollars
studies.published_words: The Rush Creek Wind Farm construction supports an estimated 2,970 FTE jobs [...] the 290 FTEs include 245 FTEs for on-site construction and interconnection labor [...] 1,840 FTEs were local revenue, turbine, and supply chain workers [...] an additional 840 FTE-induced jobs; Supports approximately 180 jobs in Colorado annually
studies.cost_words: Table 11: Total Capital Cost $698,137,648; Installed Project Cost $1,164/kW; 600 MW

studies.title: Estimated Economic Development Impacts from New Generation and Transmission in Wyoming and Colorado, NREL/TP-6A20-57411 (Lantz, Tegen and others, March 2013): the 225 MW gas plant, Wyoming's share
studies.method: JEDI Natural Gas with IMPLAN 2008 state multipliers and the Wyoming Infrastructure Authority's local shares (24 percent of construction and 39 percent of O&M spending in Wyoming, Table C3); jobs averaged over a three-year build (the cumulative figure is three times the average); dollar year not stated, taken as 2012
studies.published_words: Table 6 (annual average over three years, Wyoming, gas): project development and onsite labor 103, turbine, power generation and equipment supply chain 47, induced 40, total 191; Table 7 (Wyoming, gas): onsite 11, supply chain 16, induced 9, total 36; Table 2: Wyoming sales/use tax revenue, gas, $10,200 thousand (6 percent on capital goods and materials)
studies.cost_words: Table 1: installed cost $280 million; a natural gas-fired generation facility with a nameplate capacity of 225 MW

studies.title: The same study: the 900 MW wind plant, Wyoming's share (turbines made in Colorado)
studies.method: JEDI Wind with IMPLAN 2008 multipliers; turbines, blades and nacelles from Colorado (0 percent of turbine spending in Wyoming, 18 percent of all construction spending, Table C1); a 48.5 percent capacity factor for the generation tax; dollar year taken as 2012
studies.published_words: Table 6 (Wyoming, wind): onsite 151, supply chain 569, induced 112, total 832 a year over three years; Table 7 (Wyoming, wind): onsite 41, supply chain 121, induced 55, total 217; Table 2: Wyoming sales/use tax, wind, $74,200 thousand; Table 3: generation tax, wind, $3,800 thousand a year (the $1/MWh tax at a 48.5 percent net capacity factor)
studies.cost_words: Table 1: installed cost $1,350 million; a 900-MW wind power plant
